# rebase

Merges head (with its first-parent chain since base) three-way onto onto's head, main by default, as land merges it, and records the result as one changeset there without moving any ref: build and test that changeset, then land it with expect\_target set to result.onto, so that the landed tree is the one you tested. Pass head, base and resolutions' against as full 64-hex ids, and an idempotency\_key to make a retry safe.

```yaml
title: "rebase"
description: "Rebase a change."
since: "0.3.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
cli_command: "swarmops rebase"
envelope_op: "rebase"
request_type: "RebaseReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":false}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `RebaseReq`: `swarmops schema RebaseReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base` | string or null | no |  | Where the change starts, as a land's `base`: a first-parent ancestor of `head`; when omitted, the merge base of `head` and the head of `onto`. |
| `head` | string | yes |  | The changeset to rebase: the change's head. A revision as the caller wrote it, for the store to resolve: a ref name (`main`, `release/1.2`), a full 64-hex changeset id or a unique prefix of at least 12 hex digits, optionally followed by `~N` for the N-th first-parent ancestor. |
| `idempotency_key` | string or null | no |  | Makes a retry safe: a uuid v7, as a commit's key. The same request on the same head of `onto` is the same changeset, replayed without writing. |
| `max_conflict_bytes` | integer | no | `32768` | The most bytes of hunk text an `E_CONFLICT` report carries, as a land's. |
| `message` | string or null | no |  | The recorded changeset's message; `head`'s when omitted. |
| `onto` | string | no | `"main"` | The ref to rebase onto: `main` or `release/<name>`, which must exist. |
| `resolutions` | object or null | no |  | What to make of the paths a conflict report named, as a land's resolutions. |

## Annotations

It adds to the store and changes nothing there. Run again, a `commit` adds again, another changeset signed at its own time, unless the call carries an `idempotency_key`, which makes the same call again a replay; a `blob_put` of the same content finds it stored, and says so in its result.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `false` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `false` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `false` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `false` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops rebase`](../commands/rebase.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

### MCP

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `rebase`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops rebase`](../commands/rebase.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `RebaseReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#e_identity_required): the server runs with no identity.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops rebase`](../commands/rebase.md#errors) lists them.
